AttachmentBindingRecord.description:
Canonical sidecar fact. Construction validates the message slot before it
reaches the writer; projection never decodes or hashes a large message.

AttachmentBinding.description:
One attachment slot in the complete source message. Sparse projections keep
the original block ordinal instead of renumbering the blocks they carry.

namespace.description:
Retained even when candidate bytes are unknown. Several namespaces may
describe the same source slot without merging their claims.

exported_from.description:
Actual context of this export. A receiver retains it as a declaration,
independently of its own validated receiving members.

prior_exports.description:
Supplied prior export declarations, preserved in their original order.

candidates.description: No candidates means unknown bytes. Multiple candidates remain ambiguous.

AttachmentCandidate.description:
A complete content hash can span several stored extents. Original source
claims remain distinct even when candidate hashes happen to agree.

AttachmentNamespace.description:
Original import namespace qualified by its actual source input and chain.
This is portable provenance, not receiving-archive membership authority.

AttachmentSourceClaim.description:
Historical provenance supplied by the exporting archive. These fields never
grant access to a receiving archive's inputs, chains, or import namespaces.

namespace.description:
Unknown historical provenance stays unknown; ingress never substitutes
the receiving namespace for an original source claim.

source_version.description: Complete source message identity, independent of attachment metadata.

input.description: The receiving source input whose reading contains the message.

ValidatedMember.description:
Minted by bounded byte validation. Canonical products may preserve it;
portable bundle records carry only historical claims, never this witness.

ReceivingMember.description: Portable identity of actual receiving bytes, separate from original claims.

source_version.description: Pinned source-extent fingerprint, not the complete content hash.

acquisition.description: Receiver-owned evidence for the acquired body, independent of overlap trimming.

revision.description:
A new revision, or the current one grown by a later chunk of the
same read.

extents.description:
Where the step's new bytes sit in the revision chain, in order and
contiguous: one extent, or one per content-defined chunk of bytes
stored as chunks.

AcquisitionReceipt.description:
Original body acquisition, before overlap trimming and final source chain
assignment. Historical absence is unknown. Payload declarations cannot mint it.

chunks.description:
The body's content-defined chunks, in order, when it is stored as
chunks; empty when it is one blob.

AcquisitionRoute.description:
Receiver-minted IO evidence. Native field observation does not identify
Polylogue as its producer; producer proof is a separate post-emit receipt.

Chunk.description: One content-defined chunk of prepared bytes.

blob_offset.description: Offset into the original captured material after an exact prefix overlap.

Material.description:
Authoritative material descriptors supplied by Sinex, never hash lookups.
`extents` is the material's one committed blob, or the committed blobs of
its content-defined chunks in order.

ObservationRow.description: One look at a path that found something.

path_bytes.description: Historical observations may not have retained the original path bytes.

chain.description: A byte-proven chain prefix that is not a recorded revision endpoint.

container.description: The exact container membership established by this observation.

RawRange.description:
Original decoded source interval physically acquired, before overlap trim.
None on CapturedInput means observation metadata, not an empty raw source.

DatabaseSnapshotToken.description:
Chosen once while an actual consistent provider read is held. This nonce is
custody-only, not a provider revision, arrival order or data_version. A new
transaction, including after restart, always has a new nonce.

FileSnapshot.description:
Read from the opened provider FD before I/O, then checked against that FD
and its current path after acquisition. Encoded scratch-file metadata is not
provider identity. Missing or changed evidence yields no generation.

SourceSelector.description:
The declared input format and exact native location. Display paths and
host labels cannot identify a filesystem observation.

Timestamp.description:
A point in time as a source stated it. Unknown times are `None` at the
use site, never a zero or a guess.

Session.description:
A session's own facts. Counts and times derived from its messages live
in the index, not here.

cwd.description:
Working directories in the order the session used them. A later
correction from the tool (Claude Code `relocated`) is appended.

repo.description:
The repository the session worked in, as the tool names it (a
remote URL), when it records one.

tool_version.description: Version of the tool that wrote the session.

mode.description:
How the harness ran the session, when not interactively (Claude
Code `bg` for a background session).

aliases.description:

native ID: an AI Studio prompt read from Drive names the content key

oneOf.description: A conversation or agent run the operator started.
A session another session spawned (a Claude Code subagent).
A side conversation kept inside its parent's file.

Code `agent-acompact` file): the summarize prompt and the summary.

StepProgress.description: How far one parse step read the chain's stored bytes, or why it stopped.

oneOf.description: The step stopped before the end of the stored bytes; more remain.

not parsed, through the end of the stored bytes or not.

MessageRow.description:
A message as one input holds it. `offset` is where its first record

says (`content_ids` in the sources crate), so a rewritten input that no

parent.description: The message this one replies to, when the source records it.

reported_cost_usd.description: Cost the tool itself reported for this response, as written.

duration_ms.description: How long the response took, as the tool reported it.

production.description: How the harness produced the message, beyond its content.

signature.description:

run_by_script.description:

refusal.description: The refusal category and explanation, when the model refused.

permission.description:

request.description:

turn_origin.description: What started the turn, when not a person at the terminal (`sdk`).
